correctness.rationale: For violating i,j, own load L_i < S_ij - minweight, while L_j >= S_ij, so moving the minimum-weight shared edge of weight s from j to i satisfies L_j > L_i+s; this is a strict two-coordinate majorization improvement and lowers square potential by 2s(L_j-L_i-s)>0. Finitely many orientations guarantee termination at positive-good EFX. Equality of total loads makes Lorenz comparison valid; applying repair to any optimal orientation proves zero Schur-convex price. The asymmetric R example establishes the boundary. verify.py was executed successfully, checking 9401 finite instances, 159039 orientations and 500 seeded tests.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The two multigraph works have broader valuation domains but weaker comparison conclusions; they do not imply the zero fair-price for peak-load or arbitrary Schur-convex objectives. The Lorenz theorem in 2021 is stronger on a strict all-unit subdomain but cannot be applied to general shared weights. Existence and majorization improvement are not interchangeable.

value.rationale: A motivated structural question is whether EFX constrains egalitarian objectives when every graphical good is welfare-efficiently placed at an endpoint. The theorem gives a universal Lorenz cofinality answer, simultaneously certifying no EFX penalty for every symmetric Schur-convex load objective (and Schur-concave welfare maximization) after repair, with arbitrary heterogeneous positive goods. It is not just EFX existence or a finite census. The asymmetry example shows an unbounded price once the shared-weight premise is dropped, making the boundary substantive. Limitations are disclosed without weakening the proof.
